summary: This script runs a demo function ten times in a loop, where each iteration sleeps for 3 seconds. It measures the total elapsed time from start to finish and prints out how many seconds the whole thing took.

explanations.2: This line makes the script strict: -e exits on any error, -u errors if you use an undefined variable, and -o pipefail makes pipes fail if any command in the chain fails.
explanations.11: The {1..10} syntax expands to the numbers 1 through 10, so the loop runs exactly 10 times.
explanations.16: This captures the current Unix timestamp (seconds since January 1, 1970) before the main work starts, so we can measure elapsed time later.
explanations.19: This subtracts the start time from the end time to calculate how many seconds passed; the $((...)) syntax performs arithmetic in bash.
